reasoning_quality_informational.v1_root_problem: Billing dispute tickets have roughly doubled since August 2026 (E-05: 610→590→1180→1260) even though ticket response times remain within the 3-day SLA (E-06) and no tariff/rate changes occurred (E-03, E-04), ruling out slow handling and rate changes as causes. Billing-db shows 59% of disputed bills (1785/3025) were billed from ACTUAL, not ESTIMATED, meter reads (E-02), indicating a billing calculation/import defect affecting correctly-read bills is the best-supported driver of the majority of the surge, while the field route completion shortfall (E-01: 0.88 vs 0.95 target) accounts only for the minority ESTIMATED-read share of disputes.
reasoning_quality_informational.v2_root_problem: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled from Jul (590) to Aug (1180) and remain elevated in Sep (1260) (E-05). The best-supported mechanism: billing-config rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01 with no unit scaling (E-13), misreads the 10x finer register resolution of firmware-v4.2 meters ('0.1 m3' vs legacy 'm3', E-14) as an abnormal consumption spike and rejects an otherwise valid, before-cutoff AMI read on billing import (REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION); this explains 1184 of 1240 (95.5%) disputed ESTIMATED-read bills (E-12). Whether this same defect, rather than a separate error, also drives the larger 59% share of disputes billed from ACTUAL reads (E-02) is not yet established.
reasoning_quality_informational.ideal_final_problem: BV-17 validation rejects valid firmware-v4.2 AMI reads (unit-scale mismatch on H-MDMS-BILL) and substitutes estimates.
